subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram channel_post native/plugin commands, should configured groups[chatId].allowFrom be ignored in favor of explicit chat allow, or should sender-scoped allowFrom make channel_post commands unsupported/fail-closed with clear docs and messaging?
rationale: The current code and docs do not define this senderless authorization surface, and either option changes the security boundary for operators who try to restrict a channel by sender identity.

options.title: Fail Closed For Sender-Scoped Overrides
options.body: When a channel has sender-scoped allowFrom configured, reject channel_post commands with clear messaging and document that Telegram does not provide the required human sender identity.

options.title: Use Explicit Chat Allow Only
options.body: Permit channel_post commands from explicitly configured channel chats and document that per-chat sender-scoped allowFrom is ignored on this surface.

options.title: Pause Until Broader Bot-To-Bot Policy Lands
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer the rule until the broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work defines peer/channel identity together.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed For Sender-Scoped Overrides
recommendation.body: When a channel has sender-scoped allowFrom configured, reject channel_post commands with clear messaging and document that Telegram does not provide the required human sender identity.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history in Telegram native command and callback behavior that this decision would affect.
